crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Brain Computer Interfaces
children.blurb: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read neural signals and translate them into commands or feedback, and in medicine they span assistive communication, motor restoration, epilepsy monitoring and experimental neuroprosthetics.

children.name: Early Signals of Dementia
children.blurb: Early signals of dementia are subtle changes in memory, language, orientation and behaviour that appear years before a formal diagnosis, and the field studies them through cognitive testing, imaging, fluid biomarkers and digital behaviour traces.

children.name: Functional MRI Interpretation
children.blurb: Functional MRI interpretation covers the reading of blood oxygen level dependent signals to infer regional brain activity during tasks or at rest.

children.name: Seizure Prediction
children.blurb: Seizure prediction covers systems that estimate the probability of an epileptic seizure occurring in the minutes before it happens, which is distinct from seizure detection, where the event is identified after it has begun.

children.name: Cognitive Rehabilitation
children.blurb: Cognitive rehabilitation covers the therapies, exercises and assistive tools used to help people recover or compensate for changes in attention, memory, language and executive function after injury or illness.

sections.body: Neuroinformatics and the brain covers the use of artificial intelligence on data recorded from the human nervous system, including electrical signals, imaging, and behavioural measures. Brain computer interfaces decode movement intent from cortical activity so that a paralysed person can control a cursor or a robotic arm, and several such systems have moved from laboratory demonstrations into small clinical trials with implanted electrodes. Dementia research uses machine learning on speech, gait, and imaging to find early statistical signals that precede a formal diagnosis, though these markers remain probabilistic rather than diagnostic. Functional MRI interpretation applies deep learning to clean up scans, shorten acquisition times, and map activation patterns that would otherwise take hours of manual work. Seizure prediction models read intracranial and scalp EEG to estimate when a seizure is likely, and cognitive rehabilitation tools adapt exercises to a patient's measured performance over time.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is strongest where the data is abundant and the labels are clean, which is why seizure detection on intracranial recordings and image denoising in functional MRI are comparatively mature. Prediction is harder than detection, and no seizure forecasting system has yet shown reliable performance across patients and across months of recording. Dementia signal work is promising but unsettled, with many published models failing to generalise beyond the cohort they were trained on, and the gap between a statistical association and a clinical diagnosis remains wide. Brain computer interfaces work well in controlled settings and degrade outside them, and long term electrode stability is still an open engineering problem. Cognitive rehabilitation software is widely deployed but the evidence for durable cognitive gains is mixed, and the field has no shared benchmark for comparing systems. This site tracks 1000 medical AI models and 804 scientific models, a reminder of how much of this work sits in research rather than routine care.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages here follow the arc from signal to intervention. Brain Computer Interfaces is the most engineering heavy and the place to start for how neural activity is recorded and turned into control signals. Early Signals of Dementia and Functional MRI Interpretation sit together as the diagnostic side, one working from behaviour and the other from imaging, and a reader interested in how a model gets from a scan to a clinical question would read both. Seizure Prediction is the clearest test case for forecasting in neurology, since seizures are episodic and measurable, and it shows where prediction methods succeed and where they break down. Cognitive Rehabilitation closes the section by looking at what happens after a diagnosis, where the tools are adaptive software rather than diagnostic models. Read together they cover recording, detection, prediction, and therapy, which are the four things artificial intelligence is actually being asked to do with brain data.
